shared_context.topic: applying ointment to a pierced nipple

atoms.1: If you have a pierced nipple, applying ointment can be challenging.
atoms.2: It is essential to continue taking care of your nipple to prevent infection and promote healing.
atoms.3: Gently clean the piercing area with saline solution before applying ointment.
atoms.4: Dry the area thoroughly before applying the ointment.
atoms.5: Use a clean and sterile applicator or cotton swab to apply a small amount of ointment directly to the piercing.
atoms.6: Gently rotate the piercing to prevent the ointment from accumulating in one area.
atoms.7: Accumulation of ointment in one area can cause irritation.
atoms.8: Avoid tight clothing that may irritate the piercing.
atoms.9: Avoid tight clothing that may irritate the ointment.
atoms.10: Follow the instructions of your piercer or healthcare provider regarding ointment use.
atoms.11: Follow the instructions of your piercer or healthcare provider regarding the frequency of ointment application.
atoms.12: If you experience any signs of infection, you should consult your piercer or healthcare provider immediately.

snippets.output: If you have a pierced nipple, applying ointment can be challenging, but it is essential to continue taking care of your nipple to prevent infection and promote healing.
Gently clean the piercing area with saline solution and dry it thoroughly before applying ointment.

Use a clean and sterile applicator or cotton swab to apply a small amount of ointment directly to the piercing. Gently rotate the piercing to prevent the ointment from accumulating in one area, which can cause irritation.
Avoid tight clothing that may irritate the piercing or the ointment.
Follow the instructions of your piercer or healthcare provider regarding ointment use and frequency of application.
If you experience any signs of infection, such as redness, swelling, or discharge, you should consult your piercer or healthcare provider immediately.
